name: Concept D: Moon-anchored photon-recycling cavity
description: Exotic and speculative (TRL 2). Matches the photon-recycling cavity calculation in analysis/ideas_calc.py and docs/analyses/exotic-ideas.md: 2 kg probe, 300 effective reflections, approximately 392 MW for 714 s at 40 g, 280 km/s boost over 100,000 km, and 306.9 km/s solar escape speed. Begins co-moving with Earth on a circular 1 AU solar orbit; the Moon absorbs recoil. The short constant-power boost is integrated at the launch position, neglecting solar drift and Earth/Moon escape losses. Cavity optics, Doppler losses and mirror survival are not simulated. Showstopper: sustain 300 reflections with a 22 m, 2.7 g/m² mirror receding at 280 km/s, with nanoradian pointing and wavelength/10 surface accuracy.

events.notes: Ideal 392 m/s² (about 40 g) acceleration; 280 km/s gain without onboard propellant. Moon-anchored recoil mirror; 100,000 km boost length. Optical recycling is assumed constant. This event uses integrated thrust at launch rather than propagating the 714 s powered segment.
